articles.title: Starting in 1945, a Wisconsin builder carried materials up a rock cliff for decades; his handmade House on the Rock became a lasting roadside landmark
articles.summary: Explore the remarkable journey of Alex Jordan Jr. and his iconic House on the Rock, a blend of creativity and whimsy nestled in Wisconsin. Discover its unique features and the evolution from private retreat to roadside attraction.
articles.body: Alex Jordan Jr. began building the House on the Rock near Spring Green, Wisconsin, around 1945, and worked on a 60-foot rock formation that he had found in the countryside. A decent portion of the original structure was built by Jordan himself, who carried construction materials up the steep rock face as the project grew from a weekend retreat into a sprawling attraction.Jordan was born in Wisconsin in 1914 and had learned construction while working with his father. The House on the Rock was not designed by Frank Lloyd Wright, despite the property's proximity to Wright's Taliesin estate. The Taliesin Preservation places the two sites less than seven miles apart, and specifically notes that Jordan was neither an architect nor a member of Wright's Taliesin Fellowship.Jordan initially wanted a retreat on the rock, but the construction continued as he experimented with the building and its setting. The House on the Rock's own account says that he first rented the rock and surrounding land from a local farmer before his family eventually purchased a larger 240-acre property.The building became the attractionWord started to spread about Jordan's unusual construction project, and people began visiting. Jordan initially charged 50 cents to enter, and apparently expected the fee to discourage visitors. Instead, people paid to see the house, and the money was put back into construction and the growing collections. The project changed again when Jordan began using the income from visitors to expand the site and acquire objects for display, with the house becoming part residence, part architectural experiment and part collection of curiosities. Taliesin Preservation states that Jordan carried materials up the steep cliff and worked on the original house for decades, and the site was eventually filled with rooms and displays that extended far beyond his vision of the small retreat.The House on the Rock's own historical account says that Jordan became irritated by the attention his project attracted but ultimately embraced the public interest by charging admission. By 1960, the property was open to the public and had developed into a destination rather than a private retreat.The additions kept getting strangerThe property expanded into a much larger complex containing themed rooms, collections and architectural additions. One of the best-known later additions is the Infinity Room, which is a long, narrow structure that projects 218 feet outward from the building. Taliesin Preservation notes that it was added in 1985 and uses a large counterweight system to extend above the valley. The structure contains 3,264 windows and creates an optical effect in which its triangular floor appears to continue toward infinity.The complex eventually included attractions such as the World's Largest Carousel, extensive gardens and rooms filled with mechanical and musical objects. Jordan continued altering the property throughout his life, and later owners expanded it after his death. The House on the Rock also became closely linked with the surrounding tourist landscape of Spring Green, and its proximity to Taliesin has frequently caused visitors to assume the two properties are connected architecturally, but Taliesin Preservation states that Wright did not build the House on the Rock and that there is no evidence the two men ever met.Jordan died in 1989, but the project continued after him. It initially began with a man hauling building materials up a 60-foot rock formation in the 1940s that had become a large roadside attraction with multiple buildings, collections and architectural oddities spread across the Wisconsin property.You use AI every day. articles.title: Malaysia sends 1,476 Myanmar nationals home despite UN warnings over safety
articles.summary: Malaysia began repatriating Myanmar nationals under a voluntary programme despite warnings from the United Nations refugee agency and rights groups that
articles.body: Malaysia began repatriating Myanmar nationals under a voluntary programme despite warnings from the United Nations refugee agency and rights groups that conditions in Myanmar remain unsafe.The first group of 1,476 people began their journey and are among 5,000 Myanmar nationals who Malaysia plans to repatriate in stages, news agency AP reported. According to Malaysia's home ministry, 10,388 Myanmar nationals were being held at immigration detention centres across the country as of August 15.A ministry official confirmed the repatriation. Buses believed to be carrying returnees arrived at a stadium in Manjung in central Perak state amid tight security. Ships believed to be from Myanmar were docked at the nearby Lumut naval base.The ministry said those in the first group had agreed to return voluntarily and would be transported using two Myanmar navy warships and a hospital ship. Details about their identities and individual circumstances were not immediately available.Myanmar has been facing armed conflict and political instability since the military seized power in 2021.The UN refugee agency and rights groups have urged caution over the repatriation programme, saying security and humanitarian conditions in parts of Myanmar remain volatile and that returnees could face serious risks.Malaysia hosts about 215,600 refugees and asylum seekers registered with the UNHCR, including around 126,000 Rohingya Muslims. The country is home to one of Southeast Asia's largest refugee communities.Malaysia is not a party to the UN Refugee Convention and treats refugees as undocumented migrants.The Rohingya have faced decades of discrimination and persecution in Myanmar, where authorities have largely denied them citizenship and refused to recognise them as an ethnic group. In Malaysia, they have also faced growing public hostility amid concerns over jobs, public services, security and the size of the refugee population, as well as misinformation and inflammatory rhetoric on social media.Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim has defended the repatriation policy as a diplomatic effort to find a long-term solution. He has said Malaysia cannot host refugees indefinitely and that Myanmar must take responsibility for its citizens.Anwar said he plans to invite Myanmar leader Min Aung Hlaing to Malaysia to discuss the long-running issue of refugees and undocumented migrants.“I am inviting him to say that we can be friends and trade, we can accept Myanmar, but Myanmar must accept them back,” Anwar said in a podcast posted online on September 16. “To me, that's better diplomacy than just shouting angrily at Myanmar.”Myanmar foreign ministry official Han Win Aung said the plan follows repatriation operations in 2021 and 2022, when Myanmar received more than 1,100 of its nationals stranded in Malaysia.He said the repatriation involves genuine Myanmar citizens and is not intended to bring back Rohingya people.You use AI every day. articles.title: In 2016, an investor paid $6.5 million for an 1840s Charleston mansion turned into a bed-and-breakfast; after a three-year restoration, it was listed for $22.25 million
articles.summary: Discover the story behind the John Ravenel House, a historic Charleston mansion that underwent a significant restoration after being purchased for $6.5 million in 2016 and listed for $22.25 million in 2024.
articles.body: Scott Bessent and John Freeman bought Charleston's John Ravenel House for $6.5 million in 2016, when the historic property was being used as a bed-and-breakfast. They spent three years stripping the house back and rebuilding it with historically appropriate details before putting it on the market for $22.25 million in October 2024.The three-story house stands at 5 East Battery, which is directly along Charleston's historic waterfront. It was built around 1848 for the Ravenel family and was rebuilt after the 1886 Charleston earthquake. The historic residence had been divided into a small hotel by the time Bessent and Freeman purchased it, and the restoration therefore involved more than cosmetic changes. According to the Wall Street Journal, the owners took the house down to the studs and rebuilt portions of the interior, and undid the rooms that had been divided for its bed-and-breakfast use. The house has eight bedrooms and 10 bathrooms and sits on a roughly 0.41-acre double lot, and its second- and third-floor piazzas overlook Charleston Harbor, while the property also includes a three-bedroom carriage house, pool house, and garage.The restoration went beyond the roomsThe State reported that the project restored Greek Revival details and mantels, reconstructed brick fireplaces and reopened the ground-floor loggia. The owners also removed historically inappropriate repairs and modern additions and carried out flood mitigation work. The project was recognized by the Preservation Society of Charleston in 2021, which praised the work for its combination of craftsmanship and collaboration. The restoration team included architect Glenn Keyes, preservation contractor Moby Marks and landscape architect Perry Guillot.The house was reconfigured as a private residence instead of the divided rooms that were required by its previous form as a bed-and-breakfast. Bessent and Freeman furnished it with antiques collected from around the world. The Wall Street Journal reported that the dining room included custom wallpaper that depicted the family, their dog and historical scenes from Charleston.The restoration also involved careful attention to the property's exterior and surrounding grounds, with the owners working to preserve the character of the historic waterfront residence. The finished property retained its original architectural identity while incorporating updated systems and amenities expected in a luxury home.The $22.25 million asking price was more than three times the $6.5 million purchase price from 2016, when the John Ravenel House was listed in October 2024. The figure attracted attention because it placed the historic residence among Charleston's most expensive homes for sale. The house went under contract after roughly a month and a half on the market, and the eventual closing price was lower than the original asking price.The mansion eventually sold below its asking priceThe John Ravenel House ultimately sold in March 2025 for $18.25 million, with another $3 million paid for furnishings and fixtures, according to the buyer's brokerage. The $18.25 million property price was below the $22.25 million listing price, but the sale still represented a substantial increase from the $6.5 million purchase price nine years earlier.The house's original construction dates to the 1840s, and it survived the 1886 earthquake before being rebuilt. The later restoration addressed a different challenge of reversing changes that were made when the historic mansion had been converted into a small hotel and bringing back architectural details associated with its earlier design. By the time the property changed hands again in 2025, the restoration had become part of the home's documented history, alongside its original construction, earthquake rebuilding and years as the Pink Palace bed-and-breakfast.You use AI every day. articles.summary: Discover how designer Xorin Balbes turned a nearly 4-acre Montecito estate from $11.5 million into a stunning $32 million sale after extensive renovations and market repositioning. Explore the journey of Monte Arroyo and the luxury real estate market.
articles.body: Xorin Balbes bought a nearly 4-acre Montecito estate for $11.5 million in late 2022, and less than three years later, the property known as Monte Arroyo changed hands for $32 million, after Balbes undertook a major renovation and spent tens of millions of dollars on the property, according to The Real Deal.The estate sits at 465 Hot Springs Road in Montecito, the Santa Barbara County community that is known for large properties, secluded estates and proximity to the Pacific coast. Balbes was a developer and celebrity home designer, and bought the property in November 2022 after it had been offered for $15.995 million earlier that year. The final purchase price was $11.5 million, and at the time, the property covered 6.27 acres and included a roughly 14,900-square-foot house built in 1910.Balbes sold off about two acres during the redevelopment, which left the estate with about 3.97 acres. The house itself was later described as a 13,560-square-foot residence, with the renovation being carried out as a speculative project rather than a restoration that was intended for Balbes to occupy permanently.The renovation changed the value of the propertyThe estate was listed in June 2024 for $52 million, which was more than four times what Balbes had paid for the property less than two years earlier, and that asking price was later reduced to $42 million and then to $37.5 million before a buyer was found. The Real Deal reported that the sale closed in October 2025 for $32 million, and the buyer was not publicly identified in the report. The property had therefore sold for roughly $20.5 million more than Balbes' original purchase price.The listing history also shows how dramatically the asking price shifted during the project, since the property was repriced to $37.5 million in January 2025 after the $52 million launch. The final $32 million transaction was still nearly three times the $11.5 million purchase price, but it was $20 million below the first asking price.The house was originally built in 1910 and had been expanded over time, which included changes made in the 1970s. The property was already a large residence with an observation tower and extensive grounds when it went on the market in 2022. Balbes acquired an older estate and then repositioned it as a high-end modern property rather than constructing a completely new house from scratch.From an older estate to a $32 million saleBalbes had a history of working on high-end residential properties before taking on Monte Arroyo, and the Real Deal described him as a celebrity home designer who had previously been associated with luxury house flipping. The Montecito project followed that same model of acquiring an existing property, undertaking extensive work, repositioning it for the luxury market and selling it.The numbers make the transformation easy to track, since the original 2022 purchase was $11.5 million and was subsequently reduced from 6.27 acres to about 3.97 acres after Balbes sold off land. The renovated property was offered at $52 million in 2024, then repriced, and finally sold for $32 million in October 2025.The finished sale also shows the difference between a property's asking price and what a buyer ultimately pays. Monte Arroyo spent more than a year on the market after its $52 million launch, with successive reductions before the transaction closed at $32 million. The property had gone from a $11.5 million acquisition in 2022 to one of Montecito's multimillion-dollar luxury sales three years later, and the final price was close to three times the original purchase price, while the estate itself had been substantially altered in size and condition during the intervening period.You use AI every day. articles.title: In 2002, New Mexico mixed discarded toothbrush fragments and plastic tubing into a 2-mile interstate; it projected 25% longer life and 27% less waste
articles.summary: In 2002, New Mexico introduced a groundbreaking approach to road construction by paving a section of Interstate 25 with asphalt containing recycled plastic from toothbrushes and tubing, leading to longer-lasting roads and less waste.
articles.body: A two-mile section of Interstate 25 in New Mexico was paved with an asphalt mixture that contained recycled plastic in 2002, and included material from discarded toothbrushes and plastic tubing. The project was developed by Albuquerque-based TEWA Technology and used what the company called "plasphalt," which is a proprietary mixture of asphalt and recycled plastic. Wired reported at the time that the material was expected to last 25% longer than conventional asphalt while diverting 27% of the waste that is used in the process from landfills.Wired described purple fragments from toothbrushes and green pieces of tubing mixed into the road material, and TEWA's local suppliers included Philips Semiconductors, Intel, Coca-Cola and Sandia National Laboratories, which gave the project access to industrial plastic waste that might otherwise have required another disposal route. Gary Fishback was one of the inventors named on U.S. patents that covered plastic asphalt paving material. A 1999 patent described a paving material that contained recycled plastic and could supplement or replace part of the rock aggregate that is normally used in asphaltic concrete. The patent covered plastics from several waste streams, including discarded articles and containers.The road was part of a bigger waste experimentThe concept behind plasphalt was to take plastic that had little or no useful destination and incorporate it into a material that has already been used on roads. The patent described mixtures that contained at least 5% recycled plastic, with a preferred range of 5% to 20% in the patented formulation. The plastic could be granular material that supplemented or replaced some of the aggregate in the paving mixture.Ciel Bergman is an artist and Fishback's former partner, who had developed the idea of using discarded plastic in road construction after working with plastic waste that has been collected from beaches. Records from the Nevada Museum of Art describe Bergman's earlier interest in recycling waste plastic and the subsequent work by Fishback, Hal Stelmar and Dennis Egan to develop and patent the paving material.TEWA was presenting plasphalt as both a road material and a way to redirect waste by the time the I-25 section was installed, and Wired reported that the mixture cost about 10% more than conventional asphalt at the time. The company said that the material could last 25% longer, and also said that 27% of the waste that is incorporated into the process was diverted from landfill and instead used in the highway.Those figures need to be read as claims reported about the technology at the time, rather than as the result of a modern independent lifecycle study. The Wired report described the expected performance of the proprietary mixture, while the patent established the technical concept and its intended composition. Neither source provides a long-term independent assessment of the particular two-mile I-25 section that would establish how it performed over decades.Plastic had already been part of the road's designFishback and his collaborators had spent years developing the material before the New Mexico installation. Two U.S. patents were issued for plastic asphalt paving material in the late 1990s, which covered methods for incorporating recycled plastic into paving materials. The later 1999 patent specifically described recycled plastic as a component that could supplement or replace conventional aggregate.Bergman's work with discarded plastic preceded the road technology, while Fishback and other collaborators translated the idea into a patented paving material. The Nevada Museum of Art's archive includes documentation related to the project, including samples of plasphalt, source plastics, patent paperwork and field-testing material. The 2002 I-25 installation therefore represented the field use of a technology that had already been patented and tested as a way to combine road construction with the disposal of difficult plastic waste. At the time, the project provided a different use for materials as ordinary as toothbrush fragments and discarded tubing: a highway surface rather than a landfill.You use AI every day. articles.title: An Illinois waterfall and canyon photographed as a tourist attraction in 1903 remained largely closed to the public for generations; its corporate owner has now donated more than 50 acres so it can become a public park
articles.summary: A more than 50-acre property containing a waterfall, canyon and sandstone walls in North Utica, Illinois, could eventually become a public park after its
articles.body: A more than 50-acre property containing a waterfall, canyon and sandstone walls in North Utica, Illinois, could eventually become a public park after its corporate owner donated the land to the village. Covia transferred ownership of the Clark’s Falls property to the Village of North Utica on Saturday, opening the way for officials to begin planning how the natural area could be preserved and made accessible.The property includes Clark’s Falls, a significant main waterfall, an upper falls and a deep canyon surrounded by towering sandstone walls, according to CSRwire. The landscape has similarities to the natural scenery found at nearby Starved Rock and Matthiessen state parks, although the property has its own geological features and landscape.For the village, the donation marks the beginning of a longer process rather than the immediate opening of a new recreational site. Officials will now have to examine how people could safely access the property while protecting the landscape. They will also need to consider trails, parking, infrastructure, environmental protection and the cost of maintaining the site over time.Clark’s Falls has a long connection with North Utica. Historic photographs and postcards show the waterfall as a local scenic attraction as early as the beginning of the 20th century. A photograph taken in 1903 is preserved by the Library of Congress, showing that the falls were being documented as a place of interest more than a century ago.The history of the property is also connected to the early development of Utica. James Clark arrived in the community in 1833 and later became involved in several parts of its development. His work included involvement with the Illinois and Michigan Canal and Utica’s early cement industry. He also held several civic positions in the community.That history is one reason village officials see the property as more than a piece of undeveloped land. With ownership now transferred to North Utica, the village has the opportunity to decide how the site could fit into the community while retaining its natural and historical character.“Having grown up here and spent my life in Utica, I know how special this property is and what it has meant to generations of people who have known about Clark’s Falls,” Utica Mayor David Stewart said.“This is an extraordinary donation and I cannot thank them enough. To now see this land come into the Village’s ownership and stewardship is something I don’t think any of us should take lightly. There is tremendous potential here, but we also have a responsibility to approach it thoughtfully and make sure we get it right,” he said.Village to study how the property can be usedThe village plans to create a strategic planning committee to examine the property and determine what would be needed before any part of it could open to visitors. The committee will look at possible development and preservation needs, funding opportunities and the steps required to move forward.Public access will be one of the issues under consideration. Officials will also examine possible trails, parking and safety measures. Environmental protection, infrastructure and long-term maintenance will form part of the planning process as well. No final plan for a park has been approved, and there is currently no opening date.The village has described the donation as an opportunity that could shape North Utica for years to come. The community is already known as a gateway to Starved Rock State Park and the wider Starved Rock Country region. Village leaders said Clark’s Falls could eventually give residents and visitors another reason to spend time in North Utica.However, the proposed park is not intended to simply duplicate nearby attractions. The village said the property has its own natural features and could complement the outdoor destinations already present in the surrounding area.“This could be one of the most significant opportunities Utica has had in decades,” Stewart said. “But today is about the first step. Covia has provided the Village an extraordinary opportunity. Now our job is to bring the right people together to develop a plan to make the park become a reality,” he added.Clark’s Falls remains closed to visitorsDespite the land transfer, people cannot visit Clark’s Falls as a public attraction yet. The property has not been developed for recreational use and does not have the trails, safety infrastructure or other improvements needed to accommodate visitors.The Village of North Utica has asked residents and visitors to follow all posted closures and stay away from the property until it is officially opened. People who enter the closed property could face ticketing.The village said it will provide more information about the strategic planning process and opportunities for public involvement as the plans develop.You use AI every day. articles.body: NEW DELHI: DMK on Tuesday said it would not attend the INDIA bloc meeting scheduled for September 30, asserting that it is no longer part of the opposition alliance after Congress broke ties with it and extended support to Vijay's TVK following the Tamil Nadu assembly elections.DMK spokesperson TKS Elangovan said several parties were reluctant to attend the meeting due to differences with Congress. However, he said that the party is "ideologically" united and shares the objective of opposing Bharatiya Janata Party."Congress had chosen TVK in the state for the sake of two ministerial berths. So, we could not. They have said that they will continue with TVK. They are not in our alliance. How can we support them? How can we go to the meeting called by them," Elangovan said."Many of the parties there do not want to go with Congress, but ideologically, they are united. They share the same view and will oppose the BJP. Therefore, they do not need to attend an INDIA bloc meeting because every party knows the issues and is in line with the Congress. Attending the meeting alone is just a formality," he added.DMK had also skipped the INDIA bloc meeting held in June. However, the party later signed a letter to Chief Justice of India Surya Kant over the Election Commission's Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and other election-related issues.Meanwhile, Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav will also miss the meeting as the party has called a state-level farmers' conference in Lucknow. A senior SP leader will attend the meeting on behalf of the party.However, Elangovan blamed Congress for Akhilesh's absence and said, "He (Akhilesh) is also skipping the meeting. That is because of Congress. They had chosen TVK in the state for the sake of two ministerial berths. So, we could not... They have said that they will continue with TVK. They are not in our alliance. How can we support them? How can we go to the meeting called by them."Earlier on Monday, Congress general secretary KC Venugopal said Yadav had a prior engagement related to Rajya Sabha election nominations."Well, that Rajya Sabha election nomination is there. That's what he told the Congress president. Senior leaders from his party, all other seniors are coming. And we will decide what the next course of action is in the meeting," he said.Venugopal also said the Congress's next course of action would be discussed at the upcoming meeting.Uttar Pradesh deputy chief minister Keshav Prasad Maurya also took a jibe at Akhilesh Yadav's absence from the upcoming meet, saying the opposition would lose the upcoming state polls whether it contested the elections together or separately."Even if these three parties (Congress, SP, and BSP) contest the 2027 elections together, they will lose; if they contest separately, they will still lose. The BJP will form the government for a third term, so it makes no difference to the BJP which meetings they attend or skip. Furthermore, the subject of their meeting is utter nonsense. When they win an election, the very same issue becomes valid for them," he said.Meanwhile, the opposition alliance is set to hold a high-level meeting to discuss the SIR process amid recent reports of differences within the Election Commission.The meeting is also expected to discuss a proposed removal motion against Kumar, including the possibility of collecting signatures from opposition MPs.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Meet Kameirah Johnson, 18, the Renton, Washington student who won Doodle for Google from more than 10,000 entries, earning a $55,000 scholarship and a $50,000 technology package for her school
articles.summary: For millions of people, the Google homepage is part of the daily routine.
articles.body: For millions of people, the Google homepage is part of the daily routine. For 18-year-old Kameirah Johnson, it became something much more personal when her artwork took over the search engine's familiar logo and turned her idea into a nationwide celebration of identity, family and self-expression, states an online report by Geekwire. The Renton, Washington, student and Lakeside School senior has been named the winner of the 2026 Doodle for Google contest, beating thousands of entries from students across the country, adds the report. Her winning artwork is now featured on Google's homepage, giving her work an audience far beyond the classroom.A tribute to hair, identity and familyThis year's Doodle for Google theme asked students to complete the idea, "My superpower is …" Johnson answered with a concept deeply connected to her own experience: hair. Her winning piece, titled Hair Power: The Crown That Grows from Us, uses hair as a symbol of identity, heritage and inherited strength. The artwork shows three figures lying in grass, their elaborate hairstyles shaped like crowns, explains the online report.The figures are inspired by Johnson, her mother Simone and her sister Kalieyah. The composition reflects the importance of family in her creative vision and the role her mother played in helping her embrace her natural hair and cultural identity while growing up.Johnson's artwork stood out among more than 10,000 submissions and earned her a place among the five finalists announced in April, states the report. Her final selection was revealed in the month of June during an appearance on the TODAY show in New York.A scholarship and technology packageWinning Doodle for Google comes with more than national recognition. Johnson received a $55,000 college scholarship to support her next chapter, while Lakeside School received a $50,000 technology package. The prize arrives at a particularly significant moment for Johnson, who is preparing to leave Washington for college this fall, informs the online report.She will attend New York University, a school she has reportedly considered her dream college since she was 11. Her academic plans combine two interests that have shaped her ambitions: economics and studio arts. The combination reflects her broader interest in bringing creativity and business together. Eventually, she hopes to open her own gallery.From the Google homepage to a bigger canvasDoodle for Google is now in its 17th year and has become a major platform for young artists, giving students the chance to see their work displayed alongside one of the world's most recognizable digital brands. Washington has produced several recognized entries in recent editions. Mahee Chandrasekhar of Redmond High School was the state's winner in the 16th contest, while Bellevue's International School student Rebecca Wu had her artwork recognized in 2023. For Johnson, the 2026 win places her in that growing group while giving her artwork a much larger stage.Images Courtesy: Google Doodle and South Seattle EmeraldYou use AI every day. articles.title: A London artist spent decades covering his home with thousands of broken dolls, false teeth and other discarded objects, turning it into a museum of found art
articles.summary: A London artist has spent decades turning his home into a dense and colourful record of his life, covering walls, ceilings and outdoor spaces with
articles.body: A London artist has spent decades turning his home into a dense and colourful record of his life, covering walls, ceilings and outdoor spaces with thousands of discarded and collected objects. Stephen Wright’s House of Dreams in East Dulwich began as a creative project in the late 1990s but gradually became something far more personal. Broken dolls, false teeth, glasses, bottles, ceramics and handwritten memories now form an ever-growing environment shaped by travel, relationships, grief and everyday experiences. Instead of simply decorating his home, Wright has used the space to preserve memories and give unwanted objects a new place to belong.London artist turned his home into the House of DreamsAccording to Wright’s own House of Dreams website, the museum began in 1998 and was initially inspired by the television programme Journeys into the Outside, presented by Jarvis Cocker. The programme introduced Wright to outsider art environments and helped spark the idea of transforming his own surroundings into something permanent.According to RawVision, which profiled Wright’s work in 2015, he started it with his former partner Donald Jones. The pair had visited unusual artistic environments, including the Maison Picassiette in Chartres, France. Those experiences helped shape Wright’s desire to create a lasting work rather than something that would simply be used and discarded.That motivation was connected to his earlier career. Before creating the House of Dreams, Wright had worked for years as a fashion, knitwear and stationery designer. RawVision explains that he had become tired of the temporary nature of design, where objects such as wrapping paper could be used and thrown away. The house offered him a way to make something permanent.A home transformed by thousands of discarded objectsThe result is a home where ordinary discarded objects have become part of the artwork. Wright’s website says he mosaics, sticks and stitches objects into walls and ceilings, while thousands of other pieces are arranged throughout the museum and garden.Broken dolls are among the most striking elements. Wright says thousands of them are present in the museum and garden, with many collected during trips to Budapest, Prague and Madrid. The objects are not treated simply as decorations. They have individual histories and are incorporated into sculptures, shrines and larger arrangements.There are also collections of glasses bought from junk markets in Paris and tooth molds donated to the museum. One particularly personal object is a small black purse that belonged to Wright’s mother. After her death, he found miniature light bulbs and pieces of crumpled silver paper inside it. Rather than throwing them away, he kept them as they were and attached them to one of the sculptures.The house also contains objects connected to Wright’s childhood. His website describes a battered blue and white lion that his father dug up in the family garden in Shavington when Wright was a child. Other pieces have travelled much further before finding their way into the collection.The collection became a record of Wright’s lifeThe House of Dreams gradually moved beyond being an experiment in colour and objects. RawVision describes how the deaths of Donald and both of Wright’s parents, occurring only a few years after the project began, changed what the house meant to him.Wright took a short break from the work following the bereavements, but eventually returned to it. RawVision says that continuing the project became an outlet for healing and dealing with what had happened. The house became a place where memories could be held physically.That personal history is visible in the handwritten memory boards spread throughout the museum. Wright explains on his website that they record important events, thoughts about life, conversations overheard on public transport and political observations. Together, the objects and writing turn the building into something resembling a diary made from physical things.Backstory of discarded objects that became part of Wright’s homeThe objects in the House of Dreams often carry meaning because of where they came from. A doll bought after being run over by a car became part of a shrine. Two doll heads bought together at a flea market in Paris were transformed into a sculpture of Siamese twins. A red glitter-faced doll was made for a 2014 Mencap exhibition before becoming part of another shrine.Wright’s collection also extends to family-related pieces. His website describes two sculptures as part of his family. Even a ponytail donated in January 2016, once belonging to actor Richard Ashton, has found a place within the house. This approach gives the discarded objects a second existence.What does the House of Dreams represent todayFor Wright, the museum is closely tied to ideas of love, loss, childhood, trauma, travel and joy. His website describes it as a home for the discarded and unwanted.The house also reflects places that have mattered to Wright. His website highlights his love of travelling, particularly in India and Mexico, as well as his connection to Paris. Many objects in the museum were collected from those places, bringing pieces of his travels into his London home.The project is still not presented as a finished artwork. Wright acknowledges that he does not always know exactly what he is doing or why. What matters is the continuing act of creating.The House of Dreams has also been planned as something that will outlast its creator. Wright’s website states that the museum has been bequeathed to the National Trust of Great Britain.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: A Colorado rancher spent $50,000 fighting oil infrastructure he did not want on his 7,000-acre ranch; after nearly a decade, officials approved a wind project that lets his family finally earn from energy on its own land
articles.summary: A Colorado rancher who spent $50,000 fighting oil infrastructure on his 7,000-acre property has won approval for a wind project on the same land.
articles.body: A Colorado rancher who spent $50,000 fighting oil infrastructure on his 7,000-acre property has won approval for a wind project on the same land. Weld County commissioners voted 3-2 on Wednesday to approve the project, nearly a decade after oil development began affecting his ranch.According to Cowboy State Daily, Scott Salo bought the ranch in northern Weld County in 2014 after running a farm and feedlot in Torrington, Wyoming, with his wife for almost 15 years. The family moved to Colorado to ranch and rebuilt the property, including facilities for their cattle.In 2017, an oil company approached Salo about placing drilling infrastructure on his property. The company wanted to reach oil and gas reserves beneath neighbouring properties through horizontal drilling. Those properties had conservation easements limiting surface disturbance, so the well pads had to be placed on Salo's land.Salo opposed the drilling, but the minerals beneath his property had already been sold by the previous owner. This created a split estate, meaning Salo owned the surface but not the minerals below it. A two-year legal fight followed and cost him $50,000.Years of oil developmentSalo said oil company lawyers pressured him to sign an agreement allowing the infrastructure and offered little compensation for the disruption.“They threatened and threatened and threatened,” Salo said. “We were just fortunate enough to have a super powerful attorney that I guess struck some level of fear into them. But when you don't own the minerals beneath you, you only have so much leverage.”His lawyer eventually negotiated an agreement allowing the drilling pads to remain. Salo said the payments he receives are small compared with the royalties collected by mineral owners and neighbours.“The rules are all girded in favor of oil and gas,” Salo said. “I'm not against oil and gas. But this about destroyed me as a person, because you feel really helpless.”More than 350 acres of his ranch are now mapped for roads, well pads and compressor stations, according to Salo. He said pump jacks and tank batteries are visible from his home and there is traffic on the property throughout the day.“Every day, 24/7, there's traffic on and off our ranch,” he said. “When you didn't want them there in the first place, it’s an unpleasant experience. Let's put it that way.”That experience influenced how Salo viewed another energy project when a wind developer approached him in 2023.Wind project brings new opportunityChalk Bluffs Wind LLC, a subsidiary of Utah-based Enyo Power Partners, approached Salo about leasing part of his ranch for its Chalk Bluffs Energy Project.The planned development covers roughly 25,000 acres and includes 79 wind turbines in Weld County and about a dozen more in Laramie County, Wyoming. At full build, it could include up to 380 megawatts of wind power, 425 megawatts of solar power and 500 megawatts of battery storage.Salo agreed to lease about 18 acres. However, opposition soon emerged through a campaign called Save the Chalk Bluffs. Opponents raised concerns about pronghorn migration, raptors, bats, views and the area's agricultural character.The developer said the project was designed to avoid state and federal raptor nest buffers and would leave a wildlife corridor more than two miles wide. Colorado Parks and Wildlife recommended moving four turbines farther from the escarpment.Nearby landowners also objected, saying the project could fragment habitat for raptors, elk, mule deer and pronghorn, while affecting views and grazing land.Rancher says wind can support his daughtersSalo said oil and gas development had already changed his land while allowing neighbouring ranchers to benefit financially from their mineral rights.“How is it ok for them to extract the energy they're getting paid for and disturb the surface on us, but it's not ok for us to sell wind?” Salo asked. “My neighbors have been able to bring their kids home through oil and gas royalties.”He said wind income could help his own daughters continue the family ranch. “Two of our three girls, they have straight A’s but they don't want to go to college,” Salo said. “They want to do what we're doing. We’re trying to think about the next generation and the generation beyond that.”He said the lease income could help him buy more land and cattle so his daughters can return to the ranch without taking on decades of debt.“That's why we're losing so many agricultural young people,” Salo said. “The kids want to come back, but there's just there's nothing there for them.”Commissioners split over approvalNearly 50 people testified during a nine-hour county hearing, with most urging commissioners to reject the project.Commissioner Jason Maxey voted against approval. He said the application met many requirements but questioned whether the project fitted the surrounding area and the county's plan to preserve agricultural land.“It was a great application,” Maxey said. “They checked all the boxes, but it is still incumbent on us as commissioners to ensure that the application and the proposed use actually fits into our code and works with the surrounding area.”Commissioner Kevin Ross voted for the project. He said the developer had made voluntary commitments to reduce its effects on neighbouring properties.“They had done more stuff that was voluntary and not even required in our code than I had ever seen in any submission before,” Ross said. “Therefore I thought it was compatible with the area and a great project.”The 3-2 approval clears the biggest local hurdle, but construction cannot begin yet. Enyo still needs to complete engineering work, utility agreements and other approvals.Salo expects construction could be one or two years away. He plans to continue raising cattle around the turbines and hopes the wind income will help keep his daughters connected to the family ranch.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: 'Technical issue': Pakistan blocks airspace for Russian flight carrying uranium for Bangladesh nuclear plant
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Pakistan has denied airspace clearance to a Russian cargo flight carrying nuclear fuel for Bangladesh's Rooppur nuclear power plant, delaying
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Pakistan has denied airspace clearance to a Russian cargo flight carrying nuclear fuel for Bangladesh's Rooppur nuclear power plant, delaying the scheduled arrival of uranium for the facility's Unit 2. Pakistan later described the matter as a "technical and procedural" issue involving flight routing and airspace permissions.The nuclear fuel was scheduled to arrive in Bangladesh on September 24 but did not reach the country after the aircraft was not allowed to use Pakistani airspace. Russia has now proposed the first week of October as a new arrival date, according to Bangladesh officials as cited by news agency ANI."We heard that a cargo plane carrying uranium for the Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant in Bangladesh was scheduled to arrive on September 24. However, the flight was not given permission to use Pakistani airspace, so the uranium did not arrive in Bangladesh as planned. As of now, the exact reason for Pakistan not granting the airspace clearance is still unknown", ANI quoted Bangladesh's minister for science and technology Faqir Mahbub Anam saying."A new date has been proposed, with Russia indicating the first week of October for the uranium to arrive in Bangladesh", he added.Sheikh Mohammed Tauhidul Islam, joint secretary in Bangladesh's science and technology ministry, said preparations had been completed at the airport before officials were informed that the airspace was unavailable."We had completed all the preparations at the airport and were waiting, but the liaison officer from Rosatom told us that the airspace was not clear. So we couldn’t send it. It may need to be rescheduled", he said.Pakistan's high commission in Dhaka, in a clarification, said the matter was related to technical and procedural arrangements."Pakistan maintains an unwavering commitment to international diplomatic norms and processes all requests for diplomatic flight and overflight clearances within a standardised, predictable timeframe, strictly in accordance with our established regulatory guidelines and civil aviation protocols," ANI quoted it as saying."With regard to the reports being quoted, the matter appears to relate to technical and procedural arrangements concerning flight routing and airspace permissions, which can occasionally require coordination among the relevant aviation and other authorities and may result in adjustments to flight schedules", it added.The high commission also said the incident should not be linked to Pakistan-Bangladesh ties."Pakistan attaches high importance to its relations with Bangladesh, and it would therefore be appropriate to view the matter in its proper technical context and not attach undue significance to reports or narratives that may seek to misplace it to undermine our bilateral relations," it said.The Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant, Bangladesh's first nuclear power facility, is being built with technical assistance from Russia's state nuclear corporation Rosatom. The project comprises two VVER-1200 reactor units with a combined capacity of 2,400 MW.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Revanth Reddy's Ram-Shiva remarks: Congress defends Telangana CM as BJP demands apology
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Congress on Tuesday defended Telangana chief minister Revanth Reddy for drawing a contrast between Lord Ram and Shiva, saying that the remarks
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Congress on Tuesday defended Telangana chief minister Revanth Reddy for drawing a contrast between Lord Ram and Shiva, saying that the remarks were directed against Bharatiya Janata Party which is doing politics "in the name of Lord Ram."Congress Telangana chief Mahesh Kumar Goud said that BJP is trying to own Lord Ram and fetch votes in the elections and said that it is not a good practice."What Revanth Reddy has said is that Lord Ram looks rich because of his clothing, while Lord Shiva looks very poor. Physically, when we see both the Gods, one feels that Shiva represents the poor and Lord Ram represents the rich. But both the Gods are the same to us, and we pray to both the Gods. But unfortunately, the BJP is doing politics in the name of Lord Ram. The BJP is trying to own Ram and fetch votes in the elections. This is not a good practice," Goud said."Why should he (CM Revanth Reddy) apologise? I'm defending Revanth Reddy. Look-wise, Lord Ram wears a lot of ornaments. He looks rich, whereas Lord Shiva, with no clothes, physically looks poor. That is the difference. But we have affection for both the Gods, we pray to them, and we wish that both the Gods bless us," he added.This comes after Reddy on September 28 claimed that Congress had succeeded only in the southern states but struggled in the north because the BJP had "stolen Lord Ram", who is revered there, while Lord Shiva is worshipped in the south.Speaking at an interactive session organised by a media organisation in Delhi, Reddy also claimed that Shiva was the God of the poor, Ram was the God of the rich, and the BJP was a party of the rich.Meanwhile, Reddy's remarks strong response from Union minister Sanjay Kumar Bandi, who accused the Telangana chief minister of creating political divisions between Lord Ram and Lord Shiva.In a post on X, Bandi said Reddy, who had earlier remarked that “Muslim is Congress, Congress is Muslim”, was now “drawing political boundaries between Lord Ram & Lord Shiva”."Being the CM of Telangana that has Dakshina Kashi at Vemulawada and Dakshina Ayodhya at Bhadrachalam, Revanth Reddy should know better than to divide Lord Rama and Lord Shiva into North and South," he said.Telangana BJP president N Ramchander Rao also criticised Reddyand said, "Revanth Reddy's statement with regard to Ram and Shiv and comparing that Ram belongs to the rich and Shiv belongs to the poor, and PM Modi always says 'Jai Shri Ram' but doesn't say 'Har Har Mahadev' is an absurd and insulting statement to the Hindu religion. In fact, it is a statement given with an intention to break the Hindu community.""Of late, Revanth Reddy has converted himself into 'Revanthuddin' because he says that Muslim is Congress and Congress is Muslim. So perhaps he must be feeling that he's still a Muslim and therefore trying to divide the Hindu community," he added.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: In 2022, Manhattan doctor Roshini Raj paid $3.95 million for a nearly 5-acre Bridgehampton estate with a replica 15th-century Buddhist temple; after $3 million in updates, she is asking $7.5 million
articles.summary: A nearly 5-acre estate in Bridgehampton, New York, featuring a replica of a 15th-century Buddhist temple has been listed for $7.5 million, Mansion Global
articles.body: A nearly 5-acre estate in Bridgehampton, New York, featuring a replica of a 15th-century Buddhist temple has been listed for $7.5 million, Mansion Global reported. Manhattan gastroenterologist and entrepreneur Dr Roshini Raj bought the property in 2022 for $3.95 million and later spent about $3 million on changes to the estate. The property was listed on September 24, according to Mansion Global.The estate was created on vacant land by a previous owner in 2002. The owner turned the site into a weekend and holiday property for his family, using East Asian design influences. The compound was built around a replica Buddhist temple modelled after temples at the Summer Palace in Beijing.The property now includes a roughly 7,800-square-foot main house with seven bedrooms, seven bathrooms and five half bathrooms. It also has a four-car attached garage, a sauna, a gym and a wine cellar. The grounds include a lagoon-style pool and spa, koi ponds, orchards, water features, ornamental bridges and pathways.The estate was also designed according to the principles of feng shui. Its gardens contain statues collected from different parts of the world, mature specimen plants and several water features. The Buddhist temple is one of the most distinctive parts of the property, with 500-year-old doors and walls covered with murals.A private estate with a templeMala Sander of the Corcoran Group, who listed the property, described the estate as highly private because it sits on a little-known street. She also pointed to the size of the property, noting that most lots in Bridgehampton are only about one to one-and-a-half acres.“It’s insanely private,” Sander said as quoted by Mansion Global. “It’s on a very little-known street, so nobody knows where you are. And it’s large- most of the lots in Bridgehampton are only one to one-and-a-half acres.”The grounds were designed to create different spaces around the property rather than one open garden. They include meandering paths, ornamental bridges, koi ponds, orchards and mature plants. The estate also has a lagoon-style pool and spa.“The gardens are gorgeous,” Sander said, adding that she knows of no other property in Bridgehampton that has a temple. “The plants are really beautifully curated, but they don’t need a lot of tending and upkeep.”Raj made several changes after buying the estate. One of them was the conversion of the home's sunroom into a room she called the “jungalow”. The room has an animal-print theme and connects to the dining room through a traditional moon gate that resembles a garden trellis.Raj said the design was inspired by colonial clubs she had seen in Sri Lanka. The changes were part of the wider work she carried out after purchasing the property. Mansion Global reported that she spent about a year and a half making decorative changes to the estate.Temple used for meditation and yogaThe Buddhist temple has a specific role in Raj’s use of the property. She uses the space as a meditation room and yoga studio. Its circular walls are covered with murals, adding to the East Asian design of the building.Raj said the combination of the temple, gardens and water features gives the estate a sense of calm. “The magic of this property is that from the moment you enter the gates, you are transported to what feels like a private sanctuary,” Raj said. “The gardens, koi ponds and temple create a spiritual sense of calm that is irreplaceable. It is a truly serene and soulful retreat.”The property has also been used for large gatherings. Raj said the estate became especially useful when she hosted a party marking the 10th anniversary of Tula Skincare, the company she co-founded.“There were massages in the tea house, yoga and meditation classes in the temple, a lunch in the apricot orchard and dinner on the front lawn,” she said. “It was amazing to see how the different spaces could be used to create different moments of peace and celebration.”Why Raj is selling the estateRaj is now putting the Bridgehampton property on the market as her youngest child is expected to leave for college in less than a year. Her primary residence is a condominium in Manhattan.She said the change in her family’s circumstances has made this a suitable time to sell the property. Raj also said she wants more freedom to travel and spend time in different places.“I want to be free to roam the world if I choose to, and so it seems like this is a good time to pass on this beautiful property to someone who definitely will be able to enjoy it more often,” she said.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? articles.title: US announces visa restrictions for officials blocking international child abduction cases
articles.summary: The US has introduced new visa restrictions for foreign officials hindering international parental child abduction resolutions. This policy aims to protect American children and ensure accountability for those delaying the return process.
articles.body: The United States has announced a new visa restriction policy targeting foreign officials accused of deliberately obstructing efforts to resolve international parental child abduction cases.US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the measures will apply to individuals responsible for, or complicit in, delaying the resolution of such cases, as well as their immediate family members.The policy covers foreign government officials, judges, judicial administrators and law enforcement officials, among others.Under the new policy, visa restrictions can be imposed on individuals who intentionally fail to implement or comply with laws, policies or court orders aimed at resolving abduction cases and returning children to their country of habitual residence.Rubio said the measure gives the US Department of State an additional tool to hold individuals accountable and press countries to meet their obligations.“Today, I am announcing a new policy to restrict visa issuance to individuals responsible for, or complicit in, impeding the prompt resolution of international parental child abduction cases, as well as their immediate family members,” Rubio said.The US administration said protecting American children taken across international borders and helping reunite them with their parents is a priority.Rubio said deliberate obstruction by foreign officials, judges, judicial administrators and law enforcement officials can prolong family separations and prevent children from being returned to the United States.The Department of State also works to prevent international parental child abductions and facilitate the safe and quick return of children to their country of habitual residence, according to the statement.The new policy, Rubio said, provides another mechanism under US law to promote accountability when countries fail to meet their obligations under international law.“We are committed to protecting the safety and well-being of all American children,” he said.You use AI every day. articles.title: Julia Child lived in this 1889 Cambridge home for 40 years and filmed TV shows there; its current owners paid $3.7 million in 2009, renovated it, and have now listed it for $6.475 million
articles.summary: Julia Child’s former Cambridge home has returned to the real estate market, offering buyers the rare chance to own a property connected to one of
articles.body: Julia Child’s former Cambridge home has returned to the real estate market, offering buyers the rare chance to own a property connected to one of America’s most beloved television chefs. The six-bedroom residence at 103 Irving Street is listed for $6.475 million, according to the Boston Globe. Property details on Redfin show that the current owners purchased it for $3.7 million in 2009 before renovating the historic house. Built in 1889, the Cambridge property was where Child lived for four decades, entertained friends and filmed portions of her television programmes. Although the kitchen she used is now preserved at the Smithsonian, the home still carries the atmosphere of the peaceful neighbourhood where she lived and worked. Read on to know more about it here:A home tied to Julia Child’s legacyJulia Child and her husband, Paul, made 103 Irving Street their Cambridge home after Paul accepted a job in the city in 1961. The couple remained there for about 40 years, turning the house into both a private retreat and an important part of Child’s culinary career.Child became famous through her cookbook Mastering the Art of French Cooking and later reached millions of viewers as the host of The French Chef, the influential WGBH programme. Her Cambridge home also appeared in later television projects, including In Julia’s Kitchen with Master Chefs and Julia and Jacques Cooking at Home.The house sits on a tree-lined street just a few blocks from Harvard Yard. It is part of the area often known as Professors’ Row, where historic residences, academic buildings and mature gardens create a quieter setting close to the energy of Harvard Square.Historic character meets modern renovationThe Colonial Revival-style property was built in 1889 and spans 6,321 square feet, according to its current listing. It includes six bedrooms, four full bathrooms and two half-bathrooms across three floors, along with a finished lower level. The home’s historic details include four fireplaces, spacious rooms, bay windows, built-in shelving and a grand entrance. The current layout includes a living and dining area, a family room with French doors, an office space and multiple rooms that can be adapted for guests, work or entertainment.The present owners purchased the property in February 2009 for $3.7 million, according to Redfin’s sales history. Since then, the house has been renovated for contemporary living while retaining its period character and generous proportions. Its updated kitchen is very different from the one Child used for filming. The modern space features Poggenpohl cabinetry, marble countertops, a six-burner cooktop, a Sub-Zero refrigerator and a large central island. A bright eat-in area sits beside a wall of windows, while a butler’s pantry provides additional storage, refrigeration and beverage facilities.The famous kitchen has a new homeChild’s original kitchen is no longer inside the Cambridge house. She donated it to the Smithsonian National Museum of American History in Washington, D.C., where it was preserved as part of her culinary legacy.The kitchen was especially important to Child’s television work because she filmed several programmes there. Its removal means that prospective buyers will not find the exact set where she prepared recipes for the camera. However, the property continues to carry small reminders of her daily life. The Boston Globe noted that a sticker from one of Child’s favourite local restaurants, Eat, remains visible on the refrigerator door.Listing agent Ed Feijo told the Boston Globe that the renovated property still retains a sense of Child’s presence. He described it as tranquil and relaxing, suggesting that the home’s appeal comes not only from its celebrity history but also from its calm setting and garden-oriented design.Bedrooms, outdoor spaces and amenitiesThe primary bedroom suite is located on the second floor and includes a fireplace, walk-in closet, built-in cabinetry and an ensuite bathroom with a double vanity. Pocket doors and a private balcony add to the room’s traditional character.The third floor includes two additional potential bedrooms, one of which is currently arranged as a media room with its own fireplace. There is also an office area and extensive storage. The finished lower level contains an exercise room, laundry room, half-bathroom, wine room and more storage space.Outside, the property offers mature landscaping, a fenced yard, a brick patio and two covered porches. Many of the plants were reportedly established by Julia and Paul Child themselves. The garden surrounds the home with greenery and helps explain why the property became such a long-term refuge for the couple.The residence also has a porte cochère, or covered entrance for vehicles, along with driveway parking for three cars. According to the listing, the sheltered parking area was once where Child left her Volkswagen after returning from shopping for fresh ingredients.A major increase in valueThe current asking price of $6.475 million represents a substantial increase from the $3.7 million paid by the present owners in 2009. Redfin lists the property at approximately $1,024 per square foot and records the latest listing date as September 23, 2026.The listing also highlights solar panels, Lutron lighting, central air conditioning, a wine room, professional landscaping and an irrigated garden. Its location near Harvard Yard, restaurants, museums, universities and public transport adds to its appeal beyond its connection to Julia Child.Cambridge officials have also voted in favour of installing a historical marker at the property, recognising its connection to Child and her television work. For the next owner, the house would therefore be more than a luxury residence. It would be a piece of American food and television history, updated for modern life but still shaped by the chef who spent four decades making it her home.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? articles.title: New NCERT book says Indian kings received swords from goddesses to resist religion-driven invasions
articles.summary: NCERT’s new class nine social science textbook, released on Tuesday, mentions that many kings and princes received swords from goddesses such as Kali,
articles.body: NCERT’s new class nine social science textbook, released on Tuesday, mentions that many kings and princes received swords from goddesses such as Kali, Durga, and Bhavani to resist invasions since the seventh century.The chapter titled "Resistance and Resilience" in the book "Understanding Society India and Beyond-Part 2" outlines successive invasions of the Indian subcontinent since the seventh century."Annamaraja, ruler of Bastar is believed to have received his sword from Manikyadevi (Danteshvari) while Kumara Kampana (Vijayanagara) was believed to have used a goddess-given sword against the Sultanate forces at Madurai. Similarly, Shivaji is also traditionally believed to have obtained a sword from goddess Tulja Bhavani," the chapter reads.The chapter also describes religious traditions in warfare, with the worship of goddesses being a long-standing tradition.The first part of the textbook was released in June.According to the chapter cited by PTI, the subcontinent witnessed successive invasions since the seventh century which were driven by territorial expansion and religious motives.It also mentions how and when Indian rulers and communities resisted against Arab, Turkish, Mughal and European forces.The textbook also claims that Mughal brutality against Sikh gurus has few comparisons in history.According to NCERT chief Dinesh Saklani, Social Science learning at secondary level aims to encourage critical inquiry."Social Science learning at this (secondary) stage is expected to cultivate analytical and discursive abilities, encourage critical inquiry, promote intercultural understanding, and enable learners to participate with confidence and responsibility in civic and social life", Saklani said."It is in this spirit that Understanding Society: India and Beyond, the Grade 9 Social Science textbook for the Secondary Stage, has been conceptualised and developed," he added.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: 'No locus standi': India rejects Turkey President Erdogan's remarks on Kashmir at UNGA
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Ministry of external affairs on Tuesday slammed Turkish President Tayyip Erdogan for raising the Kashmir issue at the United Nations General
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Ministry of external affairs on Tuesday slammed Turkish President Tayyip Erdogan for raising the Kashmir issue at the United Nations General Assembly and said that no external party has any locus standi on the issue of India's territorial integrity and sovereignty.During a bi-weekly press briefing, MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal rejected Erdogan's remarks and said, “You would have seen that the remarks you referred to were made by the Turkey president. India rejects the unwarranted references to India and the Indian Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir made by the President of Turkey during his address to the UN General Assembly.”“This is a matter, as you would understand, pertaining to India’s territorial integrity and sovereignty, and no external party has any locus standi on this issue,” he added.Earlier, on September 22, Erdogan had raised the Kashmir issue at UNGA, saying the matter “should be addressed through dialogue.”“In South Asia, it is important that all disputes, including the Kashmir issue, be addressed through dialogue within the framework of the United Nations Charter and of relevant resolutions,” he said.Turkey has raised the Kashmir issue on global platforms in the past as well.Notably, Erdogan-led Turkey has also formed a Nato-like military alliance with two other Islamic nations, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia.The pact, known as the 'Mecca Pact', was signed between the three countries in August this year.India, however, has consistently rejected any third-party mediation in the Kashmir issue and repeatedly maintained that Jammu and Kashmir is an integral part of India.Following the Pakistan-sponsored terror attack in Pahalgam, India made it clear that New Delhi would only engage with Islamabad on Kashmir-related issues bilaterally.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Nepal rains: 27 killed in rain-induced disasters, authorities say
articles.summary: At least 27 people have been killed in Nepal by the rain related calamities since September 24, according to the authorities.
articles.body: At least 27 people have been killed in Nepal by the rain related calamities since September 24, according to the authorities.The National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority (NDRRMA) reports that eight people have been hurt in landslides and floods caused by severe rainfall, while four individuals are still unaccounted for.According to the administration, since September 24, twenty individuals have died in landslides, four in floods, and three in accidents involving severe rainfall.114 cattle were slaughtered and 1,082 households were impacted by the disasters. Additionally, 31 bridges were damaged by landslides and floods, and 227 homes were totally destroyed while 142 others were partially damaged.Between September 24 and 27, 542 rain-related catastrophe situations were documented, according to the NDRRMA.The Department of Hydrology and Meteorology reports say that over the four days ending September 27, 186 rainfall measurement stations nationwide recorded more than 100 mm of precipitation.At 544.2 mm, Dedhgaun in Nawalparasi (Bardaghat Susta East) had the most rainfall, followed by Panchase in Kaski with 500.2 mm and Atraulitaar in Tanahun with 472 mm.The meteorological experts attributed the severe rains to moisture-laden winds from the Bay of Bengal and a low-pressure region near Uttar Pradesh in northern India.Over 980,000 individuals received flood-warning SMS notifications from the NDRRMA via telecom service providers.According to NDRRMA spokeswoman Shanti Mahat, some 2,000 individuals who were at risk of flooding were moved to safer locations. According to her, a helicopter was used to rescue people, who were stranded by landslides, and floods in isolated areas including Jajarkot, Myagdi, and Baglung.For search, rescue, and relief efforts, security troops from the Nepali Army, Armed Police Force, and Nepal Police were sent in.On September 27, a helicopter rescued 78 individuals, who were in danger in Pauddhar of Annapurna Rural Municipality-5 in Myagdi and transported them to a safe location, according to Mahat. Additionally, four individuals, who were stuck on an island in Jajarkot's Bheri River were flown, according to PTI report.According to local media sources, heavy rains caused landslides in Chame, Manang, on the afternoon of September 27. Flood and landslide debris from Ghatte Khola partially blocked the Marsyangdi River, allowing the two streams to join and form a lake.As the river surged, people in Chame and the surrounding regions evacuated to caves, forests, and other safer places. According to local media accounts, a bridge that had been buried started to resurface by Monday, and the lake's water level had dropped by around a meter.Along the Kaligandaki corridor, the water also caused damage to roads and bridges. Kantipur reported that the swelling river was cutting away portions of the road and causing landslides at many sites. Near Ridi and Rudrabeni, more than 50 meters of road were destroyed, and around 30 meters of road were cut at Dedhgaun.The NDRRMA sent out notifications to local bodies and authorities in the affected districts, requesting that they remove families residing in dangerous regions to safer sites and keep a high degree of surveillance in downstream areas.According to the NDRRMA, starting on September 28, water levels in significant rivers, including as the Narayani and Gandaki, began to progressively drop and the situation was generally returning to normal.The most recent floods and landslides occur, when Nepal is still recuperating from the catastrophic flash floods that occurred close to the border between Nepal and Tibet last month.On August 26, the Bhotekoshi River, which flows south from the Himalayan border area, brought flooding downstream, destroying homes, cars, highways, bridges, and hydropower projects. Over 1,450 people were killed, and about 5,000 are still missing.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.
