articles.title: In 2005, Maria Menounos paid $2.3 million for an Encino home; 21 years of renovations later, the 5,145-sq-ft compound with a theater, studio and guesthouse is asking $6.995 million
articles.summary: Maria Menounos has listed the Encino home she shared with husband Keven Undergaro for $6.995 million, nearly two decades after the couple purchased the
articles.body: Maria Menounos has listed the Encino home she shared with husband Keven Undergaro for $6.995 million, nearly two decades after the couple purchased the property for $2.3 million. Realtor.com reports that the 1938 residence has since been transformed into a 5,145-square-foot compound with a private theatre, podcast studio, guesthouse, gym and tennis court. Set on 0.8 acres in the guarded Rancho Estates neighbourhood, the six-bedroom, 5.5-bathroom property has been designed for both entertaining and family life. It is more than a celebrity listing. Over the years, the home became a backdrop to Menounos’ television, radio and podcast career, as well as her life with Undergaro and their daughter, Athena. Read on to know more about it here:A longtime Encino retreatMenounos and Undergaro bought the property in 2005, when the media personality was building her career in entertainment. Public records cited by Realtor.com show that they paid $2.3 million for the house. After 21 years of ownership, renovations and personal changes, the couple is now offering it for almost three times that amount.The home is hidden behind tall privacy hedges and gates in Encino’s Rancho Estates enclave. Its 0.8-acre grounds give the property the feeling of a private retreat, while its large scale and multiple structures make it suitable for hosting guests, working from home and spending time with family.The listing describes the estate as a multi-structure tennis court compound created for “grand-scale entertaining” and “everyday wellness.” Andrew Manning of Berkshire Hathaway HomeServices California Properties is handling the listing.A theatrical entrance and warm interiorsThe main house combines traditional details with the features of a renovated modern property. Visitors enter through a space with checkered flooring and a grand staircase, creating a more formal first impression before moving into the home’s comfortable living areas.The living room includes a fireplace and French doors opening towards mature landscaping. The house also features an updated open-concept kitchen designed to function as a gathering space rather than simply a place for preparing meals.Dual staircases lead to the upper floor, where the secondary bedrooms are located alongside a spacious primary suite. The primary bedroom includes generous closet space, while the home’s six-bedroom layout gives the next owners flexibility for family members, visitors, offices or creative work.The private theatreOne of the property’s most distinctive features is its elaborate home theatre. In a 2017 interview with the Los Angeles Times, Menounos explained that she and Undergaro converted a former classroom into a private screening room.The theatre has 15 reclining leather seats, beds for naps, and its own bathroom and shower. Menounos said the room became such a favourite that the couple could spend entire weekends there watching films and television programmes.The estate’s entertainment spaces extend beyond the indoor theatre. The grounds include an outdoor screening area, while a separate barroom was designed by Jon Taffer, known for his work on the television show Bar Rescue. Together, these spaces make the property feel closer to a private hospitality venue than a conventional family home.Built around work and wellnessMenounos has spent much of her career working in television, radio and podcasting, so the property’s workspaces are closely connected to her professional life. A separate podcast studio and side office provide dedicated areas for recording, editing and production.Elsewhere on the compound, a detached guesthouse can serve as accommodation for visitors, a private office or a creative studio. The property also has a separate gym overlooking the pool, giving the owners a dedicated place for exercise without having to leave the grounds.These spaces reflect how celebrity homes have changed over time. Rather than focusing only on bedrooms and formal entertaining rooms, the Encino compound has been organised around production, wellness, privacy and flexible family use.Pools, courts and fruit treesOutside, the property offers a private swimming pool, tennis court and broad lawns surrounded by mature landscaping. A circular driveway leads to a substantial motor court, while covered parking areas provide space for several vehicles.The gardens also have a productive side. The property contains about 16 fruit trees, including orange, tangerine, grapefruit and lemon varieties. A brick-enclosed vegetable garden adds another touch of domestic practicality to an estate otherwise shaped by luxury amenities.The combination of greenery, recreational facilities and privacy gives the grounds a resort-like quality. At the same time, the fruit trees and vegetable garden make the setting feel personal and lived-in rather than purely designed for display.A home connected to family milestonesThe Encino residence has been part of Menounos and Undergaro’s relationship for approximately two decades. The couple began dating in 1998 and married during a live New Year’s Eve television broadcast in 2017. They later celebrated with a second wedding in Greece. In June 2023, they welcomed their daughter, Athena, through surrogacy. The home therefore represents a significant period in Menounos’ personal life as well as her professional journey.Before being listed for sale, the property was offered as a luxury rental. It appeared on the market for $40,000 per month in October 2025, with the price later reduced to $35,000. It is now being marketed for an outright sale at $6.995 million.The next owner will inherit a renovated Los Angeles compound with unusually extensive amenities. But the home’s strongest appeal may be the story attached to those spaces. It was not simply designed as a celebrity showplace. It evolved over 21 years into a theatre, workplace, family residence and private escape that reflected the changing life of Maria Menounos and her family.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? articles.title: 4 CISF personnel killed after colleague opens fire in J&K's Kathua; officer among dead
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: At least four Central Industrial Security Force (CISF) personnel, including an assistant commandant, were killed in a fratricide incident at a
articles.body: NEW DELHI: At least four Central Industrial Security Force (CISF) personnel, including an assistant commandant, were killed in a fratricide incident at a power project in Jammu and Kashmir's Kathua district on Tuesday, as news agency PTI reported citing officials.The incident took place around 7.30pm at the Sewa-III hydroelectric power project in Mashka village of Basohli, near the Himachal Pradesh border, officials said.According to preliminary information, Head Constable Abhidesh Kumar allegedly opened fire with his service rifle after an argument with some colleagues.Four CISF personnel suffered critical injuries in the firing and later died at the nearby NHPC hospital, officials said.The deceased were identified as Assistant Commandant Ankit Kumar Pandey, Sub-Inspector Lakshman Singh and constables Rafiq Ahmed and Sandeep Kumar.The accused was overpowered by his colleagues after the firing and later arrested. His service weapon was also seized as part of the investigation, officials said.Senior CISF and police officers reached the spot following the incident.Officials said the exact reason behind the argument and the circumstances leading to the firing are being investigated.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: A 9-acre Colorado ranch near Aspen has two natural hot springs that heat the house and supply its water; with half a mile of river frontage and its own geothermal system, the property is now asking $5.95 million
articles.summary: In Colorado's Crystal River Valley, some homes come with mountain views. This one comes with something far more unusual: its own natural heating system.
articles.body: In Colorado's Crystal River Valley, some homes come with mountain views. This one comes with something far more unusual: its own natural heating system. Set on nearly nine acres between Carbondale and the historic village of Redstone, Hot Springs Ranch has two natural hot springs, half a mile of private river frontage and a geothermal system that turns the property's underground heat into an everyday utility, states a Realtor report.The gated ranch at 14418 Highway 133 has recently entered the market for $5.95 million, bringing together a renovated mountain home, riverside amenities and a remarkably self-contained water and heating system, adds the online report.A home heated by the earthAt the heart of the property is a 3,445-square-foot residence originally built in 1964. The house has since undergone an extensive transformation and is now presented as essentially new, while retaining its setting among the mountains. Its geothermal system draws heat directly from the property's hot springs, providing warmth throughout the house. Another spring supplies water to the residence and also feeds a cold plunge, making the natural geothermal resource an integral part of daily life rather than simply a recreational feature. The property also comes with extensive water rights, adding another layer of practical value to the unusual setup, states the report.Inside, the main level revolves around an open living area with a wood-burning fireplace, a high-end kitchen and floor-to-ceiling windows that bring the surrounding peaks into view. The primary suite sits off the main living space and includes a designer bathroom. Two additional bedrooms and a media room occupy the lower level, alongside a large garage and workshop. There are three full bathrooms, radiant heating and furnishings included with the sale.A private stretch of the Crystal RiverThe outdoors may be the property's biggest draw. Approximately half a mile of river frontage runs along the ranch, with terraced gardens descending toward the water. At the river's edge sits a private bath house, while an elevated deck overlooks Filoha Meadows, a protected open space where elk and bighorn sheep are frequently seen. Red-rock cliffs and mountain peaks complete the backdrop. For anglers, the setting offers another major perk: fly-fishing is available directly from the property, eliminating the need to travel elsewhere for access to the Crystal River.Built for mountain livingThe Realtor report states that despite its secluded feel, the ranch has been designed with practical mountain living in mind. A pull-through driveway provides space for trailers and campers, while an RV pad with hookups offers additional flexibility. A pole barn provides storage for larger equipment, giving the property functionality beyond that of a conventional luxury retreat.The location also places the ranch near one of the area's better-known natural attractions. Penny Hot Springs, a public soaking spot along the Crystal River, is nearby. The springs' mineral-rich water reaches temperatures of about 133 degrees before mixing with the cooler river.Close to Redstone and AspenThe historic village of Redstone is roughly four miles away, with its small collection of restaurants, galleries, shops and the historic Redstone Inn. Aspen is less than an hour's drive, putting the area's skiing, dining and cultural attractions within reach while the ranch remains tucked into the quieter Crystal River Valley. With natural hot springs powering the house, private river access and nearly nine acres of Colorado landscape, Hot Springs Ranch offers an unusually literal take on self-sufficient mountain living, concludes the report.Image Courtesy: RealtorReady to Make a Smarter Property Decision? articles.title: Eiffel Tower chief to step down after female staff excluded during Hindu group's visit
articles.summary: The chief of the company operating the Eiffel Tower will leave his post at the end of the year after an independent probe found that female employees were
articles.body: The chief of the company operating the Eiffel Tower will leave his post at the end of the year after an independent probe found that female employees were excluded during a visit by a Hindu religious group earlier this month.Patrick Branco Ruivo, director general of the Société d’Exploitation de la tour Eiffel (SETE), has decided to step down following an investigation into the September 5 visit by a delegation from Bochasanwasi Shri Akshar Purushottam Swaminarayan Sanstha, or BAPS.The probe found several operational failures, including the exclusion of female staff from the visit.SETE called the situation as “in female staff being excluded from the visit that day, an unacceptable situation,” in a statement on Tuesday.The decision comes weeks after Ruivo, who took charge of SETE in 2018, faced a staff protest over the issue. The Eiffel Tower was closed on September 7 as employees went on strike.A union official had called the management instructions “unacceptable”.Employees had been told that female staff should not come into contact with the BAPS delegation, which was in Paris for celebrations marking the opening of a traditional Hindu stone temple.BAPS is a global religious and civic organisation belonging to the Swaminarayan sect, a branch of Hinduism.SETE chair Ariel Weil said the company would introduce measures and training programmes focused on gender equality.However, following the visit by BAPS officials to the iconic Eiffel Tower, the Hindu organisation clarified its position.In a statement released after the visit, the BAPS Hindu temple in Paris said it took the concerns "very seriously" and apologised for "any pain or inconvenience caused.""Due to the size of our delegation, the visit was arranged in conjunction with the Eiffel Tower team at the start of normal opening hours to avoid disrupting or inconveniencing others," it said."To the best of our knowledge, at no point was anyone prevented access to the Eiffel Tower," it added, saying it believed in the "universal values of mutual respect and service."The Eiffel Tower, which is 330 metres tall and draws around 7 million visitors each year, has faced staff strikes before.You use AI every day. articles.title: SIR row: At CWC meet, Rahul Gandhi credits Congress for EC 'revelations', gives 'oppose and resist' message
articles.summary: NEW DELHIL Leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi on Tuesday claimed that Congress's sustained campaign over alleged irregularities in
articles.body: NEW DELHIL Leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi on Tuesday claimed that Congress's sustained campaign over alleged irregularities in elections had forced differences within the Election Commission over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls into the public domain, news agency PTI reported, citing sources.Speaking at a closed-door meeting of the Congress Working Committee at Indira Bhawan, Rahul Gandhi said revelations about the poll panel were now coming out because of the party's campaign, sources told PTI.He said the Congress had been consistently raising the issue of "vote chori" and highlighting alleged irregularities in the elections in Haryana, Karnataka and Maharashtra, but had initially faced scepticism."The atmosphere has changed over the last two years," Ranhul said, according to PTI sources, attributing the shift largely to the Congress's "fact-based presentations"."The issue is now being discussed in the media and in editorials," he was quoted as saying.During the meeting, Rahul Gandhi said there were two forms of "match-fixing" in elections, one involving electronic voting machines (EVMs) and the other involving alleged deliberate tampering with voter lists."So, there are two forms of match-fixing: EVM match-fixing and voter list match-fixing, both are happening," he reportedly said.The Congress leader also claimed that the 2024 Lok Sabha election was "completely fixed and rigged".He further alleged that legislation enacted thereafter, specifically the law passed in December 2023 providing immunity to the Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners, was illegal, sources said.'Virodh and pratirodh': Rahul Gandhi's message to party workersRahul Gandhi also urged Congress workers not to deviate from the path of "virodh" (opposition) and "pratirodh" (resistance), from the streets to Parliament, according to PTI sources.Invoking the Lahore Congress session of 1929, Gandhi said the party had chosen the path of "Purna Swaraj" at a time when the British government had denied Congress even provincial autonomy.As the present government refuses to listen to the voice of the people of this country or heed their demands, there is only one way forward for parties that believe in democracy -- to resist, sources quoted him as saying.The comes as Congress demanded the immediate removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, suspension of the SIR, restoration of over 13 crore names struck off from the electoral rolls and the resignation of Prime Minister Narendra Modi for "match-fixing" polls.The meeting comes days after The Indian Express reported that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had raised objections on record at least 14 times in the past 10 months over SIR decisions and orders they said were issued without their knowledge or recommendation.Amid questions over the objections raised by the two commissioners, the EC has maintained that differing views and observations are a normal part of deliberations in any institution. It has also asserted that all its orders carry full legal sanction and follow established statutory procedures.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Auto driver held for abusing, assaulting women in Bengaluru
articles.summary: Bengaluru police arrested auto driver Chetan after HSR Layout fight video went viral; women allege abuse and assault after cancelling an app booking.
articles.body: Bengaluru: A day after the video of a fight between an autorickshaw driver and two women in HSR Layout went viral, police arrested 30-year-old driver Chetan.One of the women, in her 20s, went to the police station Tuesday and filed a complaint after cops got in touch with her. The woman told police she had booked the auto through an aggregator app and subsequently cancelled it. The driver, who reached the location, abused her and when she retorted, he assaulted her and her friend, a senior police officer said.A case has been registered under Section 74 (assault or use of criminal force to a woman with intent to outrage her modesty).The video of them fighting and exchanging blows went viral on social media Monday. HSR Layout police said they contacted the women after seeing the video and asked them to file a complaint.Chetan told police the women fought over payment. articles.title: Raj Cong chief seeks election commission probe into govt bias in urban polls
articles.summary: Rajasthan Congress chief Govind Singh Dotasra seeks state election commission probe into alleged govt bias, intimidation and misuse of officials in urban polls.
articles.body: Jaipur: Rajasthan Pradesh Congress Committee president Govind Singh Dotasra has sought an inquiry by state election commission into alleged “biased conduct”, including claims of intimidation, inducement and attempts to influence councillors, of returning officers, police and administration during the just-concluded urban local body elections.In a three-page complaint lodged Tuesday, Dotasra alleged that administrative and police machinery was used to put pressure on Congress and Independent councillors during the process of forming civic bodies. He sought an impartial inquiry and action against officials and employees found responsible.Dotasra alleged that after counting of votes on Sept 14 and elections for chairperson, president and mayor posts on Sept 21, several councillors were subjected to threats, inducements and attempts to influence their voting.“Due to biased attitude of the ruling party and the administrative and police machinery, Congress and independent councillors were lured, threatened and, in some cases, attempts were made to abduct them,” Dotasra alleged in his complaint.The Congress chief claimed that 152 FIRs and complaints were registered against non-BJP functionaries during the municipal polls. He sought scrutiny of the cases and action against the guilty if these are found to have been politically motivated.Dotasra alleged that in some places returning officers extended the voting period beyond the stipulated deadline. “Voting period was repeatedly extended beyond the prescribed time without any reasonable justification,” he alleged, adding that in some places results were announced prematurely and valid votes secured by Congress candidates were rejected.The complaint further alleged that officials from departments including GST, income tax, food adulteration and labour welfare conducted inspections at business establishments linked to elected councillors. Dotasra alleged that the action was intended to put pressure on councillors and their families.Congress cited alleged incidents in Tijara, Srivijaynagar, Suratgarh, Bharatpur, Ajmer, Pali, Sikar, Jalore, Barmer, Jodhpur, Bikaner, Churu, Sriganganagar and Nagaur, among other places.Citing Tijara municipal council election, Dotasra alleged that around 18 Congress-supported councillors were stopped by Haryana Police, disrupting their movement ahead of voting. articles.title: SC grants bail to Sanjay Badaya, Shubhanshu Dixit in JJM graft case
articles.summary: Supreme Court grants bail to Sanjay Badaya and Shubhanshu Dixit in Rajasthan PHED Jal Jeevan Mission graft case, citing completed probe and filed chargesheets.
articles.body: Jaipur: Supreme Court Tuesday granted bail to Sanjay Badaya and Shubhanshu Dixit, accused in state public health engineering department’s (PHED) alleged multi-crore corruption related to Jal Jeevan Mission, while setting aside the Rajasthan High Court orders that rejected their bail pleas.A bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu held that the investigation against the two accused had been completed and chargesheets filed. “The prosecution case predominantly rested on documentary records and electronic trails, which had already been seized and were in the custody of the investigating agency, substantially reducing the apprehension of tampering with evidence,” the court said.The case arose from an ACB FIR related to corruption in Jal Jeevan Mission registered at the Anti-Corruption Bureau police station, Jaipur, on Oct 30, 2024. The FIR invoked provisions of the Prevention of Corruption Act and IPC in connection with alleged irregularities in execution of the Jal Jeevan Mission.According to the prosecution case recorded in the order, forged work-experience and completion certificates were allegedly used by two private firms to secure around 104 tenders worth approximately Rs 979.45 crore. The ACB subsequently filed its chargesheet on April 12, 2026, followed by a supplementary chargesheet on June 29, naming Badaya and Dixit among the accused.Dixit, then secretary of the Rajasthan Water Supply and Sewerage Management Board and de facto secretary of the PHED Finance Committee, was arrested on Feb 17, 2026. Badaya, described by the prosecution as an alleged intermediary, was arrested on May 11, 2026.“Since the trial was likely to be prolonged given the voluminous evidence, 124 proposed prosecution witnesses, pending investigation against some accused and absconding accused, both the accused can be released on bail. They must join the investigation if called and appear before the trial court on dates fixed,” the court said.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Jaipur | Silver Rate in Jaipur | Bank Holidays in Jaipur | Public Holidays in Jaipur | Jaipur AQI | Weather in Jaipur | Petrol Price in Jaipur | Diesel Price in Jaipur | CNG Price in Jaipur | LPG Price in JaipurStay updated with the latest Jaipur news. articles.title: Govt school teachers to now help students with career guidance
articles.summary: Rajasthan to train govt school teachers via 10-hour DIKSHA “Career Guide” module by Dec 4 to provide career guidance to Classes 10-12, benefiting 40 lakh students.
articles.body: Jaipur: The state education department has initiated preparations for training teachers so they can provide students with information about better career options. A 10-hour ‘Career Guide’ teacher training module has been made available on the DIKSHA portal, which teachers are required to complete by Dec 4. The online training allows teachers to complete the module at their own convenience and is aimed at equipping teachers to guide students regarding higher education, employment and various career paths.Officials said that the progress regarding the training will be reviewed regularly at the district level. “Currently, career guidance facilities are available in private schools or with external experts who charge a fee. In govt schools, students are not able to get such help and for them this training is a significant initiative towards preparing teachers to provide career guidance to students. Data concerning the number of teachers who have completed the training and their progress will be compiled and recorded district-wise,” said a senior official.Officials added that the lack of career guidance is a key reason why many students opt for private schools.“This initiative is likely to help over 40 lakh students studying in Classes 10 to 12 across the state,” added the official. articles.title: Flood situation eases as Mahanadi water levels dip
articles.summary: Odisha flood situation eases as Mahanadi levels recede after Hirakud closes 8 sluice gates; rivers below danger marks, 43 ODRAF/NDRF teams deployed.
articles.body: Bhubaneswar: The flood situation in Odisha showed signs of easing on Tuesday as water levels in Mahanadi began receding after authorities closed eight sluice gates of Hirakud reservoir. Inflows from the upper catchment areas in Chhattisgarh declined too. “There is currently no major flood threat across the state’s key river basins, including the Mahanadi,” said an official release from the engineer-in-chief of water resources department Dilip Rout.The release said water levels in major reservoirs, including Hirakud, and downstream monitoring stations remained under control, with trends showing either stable or falling levels. All major distributaries of Mahanadi, including Birupa, Paika, Luna, Karandia, Chitrotpala, Kathajodi, Kuakhai, Devi, Kandala, Kushabhadra, Daya, Bhargavi, Rajua and Makara, were flowing within safe limits. The department is continuing round-the-clock monitoring across all river basins.No rainfall was reported in the state between 8:30 am and 5:30 pm on Tuesday. Earlier, Banki recorded the highest rainfall of 45 mm. IMD forecast mostly dry weather for the next three to four days. Odisha has received 316.2 mm rainfall between Sept 1 and 29 against the normal of 233.4 mm, a surplus of 35.5%.Revenue and disaster management department said 43 ODRAF and NDRF teams were deployed in flood-hit districts. District administrations continued precautionary evacuation and relief measures. No fishermen warning is in force. Flood conditions have also improved in southern Odisha. Rivers in Bhadrak, Balasore and Jajpur districts were flowing below danger levels.However, low-lying areas of Cuttack, Puri and Jagatsinghpur districts have been affected by the recent flooding. Several areas have faced floods four times this season. Six villages in Tirtol and Kujang blocks of Jagatsinghpur district remained cut off as floodwater continues to surround them. Low-lying villages in Banki and Athagarh blocks of Cuttack were also affected, with three feet of water flowing over Banki-Bilipada-Talabasta road.Flooding was reported from Gop, Balanga and Kanas areas of Puri district, where distributaries of Mahanadi pass through several blocks. “My vegetable crops have been badly damaged as floodwater entered my farm. articles.title: What archival records reveal about Jyoti Basu’s studies in London
articles.summary: For decades, West Bengal has been told a simple story about Jyoti Basu: that he went to London to study, completed his studies at University College
articles.body: For decades, West Bengal has been told a simple story about Jyoti Basu: that he went to London to study, completed his studies at University College London (UCL) and at the London School of Economics (LSE), became a barrister, returned to India, and dedicated his life to communism. But institutional records that have recently come under examination raise an important question: is that account as straightforward as it has been made to appear?Records from UCL indicate that Basu entered the institution in 1935 and that his examination status in 1939 was not recorded as “Passed.” Instead, it appears as “conditionally passed,” suggesting that he still had papers to clear before he could obtain an academic degree. UCL and the University of London have also clarified that neither institution conferred a degree upon him. The London School of Economics, meanwhile, has clarified that Basu was never admitted to or enrolled in any course there, despite his long-standing description as an LSE alumnus in various media reports.Despite not having obtained an academic degree from London, Jyoti Basu is listed among the notable alumni of the Middle Temple. Yet, unlike several other prominent alumni, his academic credentials and the details surrounding his call to the Bar are not explicitly presented in the same manner.For example, the alumni profile of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel clearly states that he was admitted to the Middle Temple in October 1910 and was called to the Bar in 1913. Similarly, the profile of Lee Kuan Yew, the first Prime Minister of Singapore, clearly records his academic degree from the LSE as well as his call to the Bar in 1950. Jyoti Basu's alumni profile, however, does not clearly state any academic degree and mentions only that he was called to the Bar in 1940 in absentia.This distinction is significant. Based on formal requests made to the Middle Temple to clarify this ambiguity, certain documents appear to indicate that Jyoti Basu was admitted to the Middle Temple in 1936 as a self-financing student and that, in 1940, he himself submitted a petition to be called to the Bar in absentia, subject to the condition that he would subsequently clear certain outstanding papers. In addition, archival documents reveal that Basu had also intended to qualify for the Indian Civil Service (ICS), but he did not ultimately qualify for the examination.These archival documents therefore leave an important historical ambiguity that should not casually be converted into the categorical statement that Jyoti Basu obtained academic degree from London. Basu's principal political contemporaries and opponents included figures such as Ajay Mukherjee, Dr. Bidhan Chandra Roy, and Siddhartha Shankar Ray—individuals with distinguished professional and educational backgrounds. Against that backdrop, the repeated public portrayal of Basu as an unequivocally qualified from London deserves careful scrutiny.For decades, those who questioned communist ideology were often dismissed as intellectually inferior or “uneducated.” Yet the historical record surrounding one of the most celebrated leaders of communist party in India may itself be considerably more complicated than the familiar political narrative suggests. There is also a broader question concerning academic standards and political double standards. Those who have spent decades pointing fingers at the educational credentials, intellectual abilities, and academic qualifications of their political opponents should be prepared to subject their own leaders to the same scrutiny. If questions can legitimately be raised about another person's degree, the duration of their education, or the circumstances under which a qualification was obtained, then such questions cannot suddenly become illegitimate when directed at members of one's own political camp.This is not an attempt to diminish Jyoti Basu's political importance, but to examine his educational history through institutional records rather than political mythology. The records examined here show that his clearly documented academic qualification was a B.A. in English, Second Class, from Presidency College, Kolkata, obtained in 1935. The question, therefore, is not whether Basu studied in UCL —he did—but what, precisely, did he complete there, and why was that distinction lost in the political narrative of his life?This case should also serve as a warning about the communist's long-standing approach to Indian history. For decades, communist intellectuals and political writers have constructed and promoted ideological narratives about India's past, often repeating selective interpretations until they acquire the appearance of established historical fact. Challenging every such narrative requires enormous time, archival research, and careful examination of original documents.If even the educational history of one of the communist's most celebrated leaders in India can contain such significant discrepancies between popular narratives and institutional records, then the many historical narratives promoted by the communist also deserve serious re-examination. People should therefore stop accepting ideologically constructed and politically convenient stories of communists about India's past as unquestionable historical truth. Indian history must be rebuilt on original records, evidence, and honest scrutiny—not on narratives manufactured to serve a political agenda.Disclaimer: Views expressed above are the author's own.

articles.title: Burnham's big reset: UK PM vows new social contract, closer EU ties
articles.summary: United Kingdom Prime Minister Andy Burnham on Tuesday unveiled an ambitious reform agenda, promising a \"new social contract for the 21st century,\" changes
articles.body: United Kingdom Prime Minister Andy Burnham on Tuesday unveiled an ambitious reform agenda, promising a "new social contract for the 21st century," changes to the electoral system and a reset in a ties with Britain's European neighbours.But Burnham acknowledged that his plans would involve difficult financial choices and could carry political risks.“Small things will not get us through what are difficult times,” UK PM said in a tough-love speech at the centre-left Labour Party’s annual conference in Liverpool.He promised more social housing, improved education and more affordable care for the elderly, while warning that the government would have to make difficult decisions on welfare and pension spending to fund some of the reforms.Anticipating criticism, Burnham said: “I have given you what you often say is missing from politics: Honesty, ideas and a clear direction for the country we all love.”A major part of Burnham’s agenda is the creation of a “national care service” that would be free at the point of use and funded through taxation, similar in principle to the National Health Service.Burnham became emotional while speaking about his own experience of the care system with his father, Roy, who died earlier this month.To help fund the service, he said the government would change the pensions triple lock from 2030, after the next general election. The current system guarantees annual pension increases based on whichever is highest among inflation, average wage growth or 2.5%.“I accept I may pay a political price,” he said. “But someone has to go through the pain barrier and rip the plaster off.”Burnham also pledged to tackle street homelessness, reduce youth unemployment and give the government greater control over privatised utilities.At the same time, he said the government would “stick to our fiscal rules to get borrowing and debt down.”“I would love to go quicker, but I have to be honest about what the country can afford,” Burnham said.Burnham said Labour would contest the next general election on a promise to replace Britain’s winner-takes-all electoral system with a form of proportional representation.He also called for a rethink of Britain's relationship with the European Union, saying “Brexit has done more harm than good” and that the UK needs “clarity about our position and the future of the continent that we live in.”Burnham said his broader aim was to “move beyond a decade of drift and division” and address the economic and political uncertainty that has followed the 2016 Brexit vote.Burnham’s first conference speech as prime minister came as Labour sought to project a more upbeat image. The party’s conference is being held under the slogan “Hope again”, with delegates appearing more optimistic than at last year’s gathering.However, the government is facing significant challenges, including security concerns and a difficult economic backdrop.Five men were arrested Sunday on suspicion of explosives and terror offences outside RAF Fairford in western England. They were released on bail Monday as police continued investigating possible links to a hostile state.The arrests prompted questions at the conference about security and potential threats from countries including Iran and Russia.Economic pressures are also looming ahead of Treasury chief John Healey’s budget on October 28. The conflict involving the US and Iran has disrupted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, contributing to higher oil prices and inflation.Diesel prices in Britain reached a record high of just under £2 a litre on Monday, according to figures compiled by the Royal Automobile Club.The next general election does not have to be held until 2029, although Labour's improved fortunes have prompted speculation about an early poll. Burnham has said he will not call one early.John Curtice, professor of politics at the University of Strathclyde, said Burnham had given Labour “a halo effect from a popular leader.”“But the challenge for this party now is to change that halo effect from the leader to the party,” Curtice said. “This party needs to make much more progress before it can contemplate the prospect of an election.”You use AI every day.
